question: Vibe Coding a Turbine Blade
content: Blake Scholl describes how hardware engineering at Boom Supersonic traditionally worked â€” engineers passing Excel spreadsheets via email, no source control, no automated testing. AI changes this fundamentally.
description: You are a hardware engineering manager who just learned that your team's aerodynamicist and structures engineer have been exchanging a 50-MB spreadsheet over email for the past six months. According to Blake Scholl, what is the fundamental problem with this workflow?
options: The spreadsheet file is too large for email servers to handle reliably and causes frequent delivery failures
Hardware engineering workflows are treated as software but lack software engineering discipline like source control and testing
Excel spreadsheets lack the native capability to model complex turbine blade aerodynamics and thermal stress
The engineers should be using dedicated CAD and simulation software instead of generic spreadsheet programs
answer: Hardware engineering workflows are treated as software but lack software engineering discipline like source control and testing
explanation: Blake Scholl explains that a lot of hardware engineering happens in Excel spreadsheets with VBScript â€” it's actually software, but treated as if it's not, with no source control or automated testing.

question: Two Engineers, One Jet Engine
content: Blake Scholl describes the new model at Boom Supersonic: software engineers create the architectures, and hardware engineers vibe-code their pieces. The result is a dramatic reduction in the team size needed for complex engineering.
description: Your VP of Hardware says you need a team of fifty engineers to design a jet engine from scratch â€” that's the industry standard. Based on Blake Scholl's experience at Boom, what counter-argument can you make?
options: Fifty engineers is actually the minimum required to satisfy FAA certification requirements for jet engine design
With software engineers creating architectures and hardware engineers vibe-coding, two engineers can design an entire jet engine
You should outsource the engine design entirely to a specialized vendor with deep aerospace manufacturing expertise
Fifty engineers is fine if you divide them across aerodynamics and structures teams that work in parallel
answer: With software engineers creating architectures and hardware engineers vibe-coding, two engineers can design an entire jet engine
explanation: Blake Scholl says with the new model â€” software engineers creating architectures and hardware engineers vibe-coding their pieces â€” two engineers can design an entire jet engine.

question: The Human-in-the-Loop Hardware Simulator
content: Max Hodak describes moving from Excel to Python models for believable simulations of physical systems. He also predicts AI will soon generate STEP files and PCB layouts, not just software.
description: You run a hardware startup that relies on mechanical and electrical engineering simulations. Your team currently uses Excel for most calculations. Max Hodak sees a three-stage progression for AI in hardware. What is it?
options: Excel â†’ Python simulations â†’ AI generating STEP files and PCB layouts
Manual drafting gave way to CAD software which then enabled 3D printing for prototyping
Spreadsheets evolved into relational databases which migrated to cloud platforms for scale
Rapid prototyping leads into iterative testing cycles which feed back into the manufacturing process
answer: Excel â†’ Python simulations â†’ AI generating STEP files and PCB layouts
explanation: Max Hodak says he moved from Excel to Python models for simulations, and predicts AI will soon generate STEP files and PCB layouts â€” coming for mechanical and electrical engineering next.

question: Software Engineers Build the Scaffold
content: Guillermo Rauch reacts to Blake's description by noting a major shift in enterprise software: no startup can sell you hardware collaboration tools anymore because companies just build what they need internally.
description: A VC pitches you a startup that builds collaboration software for hardware engineering teams. Guillermo Rauch would argue this startup faces a fundamental problem. What is it?
options: The hardware engineering market is too small to support a SaaS business with sustainable recurring revenue
Companies are now just internally coding exactly what they need, so there's no room for external tools
Hardware engineers refuse to use any cloud-based software because of strict security and IP protection concerns
The startup would need at least ten years to build a product that could compete with entrenched Excel workflows
answer: Companies are now just internally coding exactly what they need, so there's no room for external tools
explanation: Guillermo Rauch says there's no startup that builds hardware collaboration tools that can sell you anything anymore â€” internally, you're just coding the right thing you need at any given time.

question: Spreadsheets Are Lightweight Programming
content: Naval observes that spreadsheets with VBScript were successful because they approximated custom software â€” they were 'lightweight programming' for people who couldn't build real software.
description: A colleague argues that spreadsheets are simply data organization tools and have nothing to do with software engineering. Based on Naval's take, why did spreadsheets with VBScript become so dominant in engineering?
options: They were the only tools available for document collaboration and data sharing among engineering teams in the 1990s
They approximated custom software for people who couldn't build real software â€” they were lightweight programming
Microsoft Excel had a dominant marketing advantage and aggressive distribution strategy that crushed competitors
Spreadsheets are inherently superior to custom programming languages for engineering and numerical analysis work
answer: They approximated custom software for people who couldn't build real software â€” they were lightweight programming
explanation: Naval says spreadsheets were successful because no one could build custom software, so a spreadsheet approximating custom software was the best available option â€” it was lightweight programming.

question: The Thousand-Blade Problem
content: Blake Scholl details the turbine blade design problem: a blade changes shape from cold to hot, requiring conversion between aerodynamics and structures. With a thousand blades per engine, manual iteration is infeasible.
description: Your team needs to analyze how each of the thousand turbine blades in a jet engine deforms under operating temperatures. Doing one blade manually takes an engineer a full day. What does the new AI-enabled workflow allow instead?
options: It automates the analysis so you can change blade geometry and see structures and aerodynamics results in real time
It eliminates the need for physical turbine blades entirely by using advanced ceramic coatings that resist deformation
It lets one engineer analyze all thousand blades in a single day with perfect accuracy and zero risk of manual error
It outsources the structural analysis to a cloud compute cluster running specialized legacy Fortran simulation code
answer: It automates the analysis so you can change blade geometry and see structures and aerodynamics results in real time
explanation: Blake Scholl says with the new combination of software and hardware people, you can change blade geometry and see in real time the structures and aerodynamics results â€” a complete transformation from one-day-per-blade.

question: Agentic Hardware Interfaces
content: Naval suggests that hardware companies with historically bad software may skip human-facing software entirely and go straight to agentic interfaces â€” an agent accesses the hardware and you talk to it through voice.
description: A hardware startup building IoT devices asks you whether they should invest in building a polished mobile app or a web dashboard for their product. Using Naval's prediction, what alternative path should they consider?
options: They absolutely need a polished mobile app with intuitive navigation to reach consumers in today's competitive market
They should build both a web dashboard and a mobile app to provide maximum coverage across all user platforms
They could skip human-facing software entirely and let agents access the hardware through voice interfaces
They should license their API to larger companies that already have customer-facing front-end infrastructure built
answer: They could skip human-facing software entirely and let agents access the hardware through voice interfaces
explanation: Naval says it 'may not even be software with a human front end â€” it might just be completely agentic, an agent accessing it, and you talk to it through voice to control hardware.'

question: You Always Want the Smartest Model
content: Naval argues that intelligence is an 'unalloyed good' â€” you always want more of it. When models make mistakes, you don't know it, and they're always cheaper than a real person.
description: Your CFO proposes using a cheaper, less intelligent AI model for 97% of coding tasks and only using the frontier model for the hardest 3%. Based on Naval's argument, what is the flaw in this cost-saving strategy?
options: The cheaper model actually costs more in total compute because it requires many more attempts to reach correct answers
When the cheaper model makes a mistake, you won't know it, and intelligence is too valuable to compromise on
The cheaper model is actually more intelligent than the frontier model for specialized coding and domain-specific work
The proposed cost-saving strategy would violate the AI model's terms of service for commercial and enterprise use
answer: When the cheaper model makes a mistake, you won't know it, and intelligence is too valuable to compromise on
explanation: Naval says: 'When these models make a mistake, you don't know it' â€” and intelligence is an unalloyed good. Given the leverage poured through decisions, you always want the most intelligent model.

question: The Two-Tier Model Strategy
content: Guillermo describes a practical split: use frontier models for pushing the coding frontier, and use cheaper models (including Chinese models and Gemini) for support tasks, browser automation, and industrial production.
description: You are designing an AI deployment strategy for your company. You need both cutting-edge code generation and cost-efficient automation for routine tasks. How does Guillermo Rauch suggest splitting the workload?
options: Use a single unified model for every single task to keep the system architecture simple and reduce operational complexity
Use frontier models for pushing the coding frontier and cheaper models like Gemini or Chinese models for support and automation
Use only open-source models exclusively to avoid vendor lock-in and maintain full control across all deployment environments
Always use the cheapest available model for all tasks and simply accept the lower quality output across the entire organization
answer: Use frontier models for pushing the coding frontier and cheaper models like Gemini or Chinese models for support and automation
explanation: Guillermo says: 'Any time I'm working to push the frontier, you need the best possible coding model. That's basically two or three models. The Chinese are certainly not in it.' For other tasks, cheaper models work fine.

question: The Monopoly Problem
content: Naval acknowledges that his preference for the most intelligent model is 'not great news' because it concentrates power among the top two or three frontier labs, creating a monopoly or oligopoly situation in AI.
description: A policy maker is concerned about AI market concentration. You explain Naval's argument that everyone will gravitate toward the single most intelligent model. What market structure does this predict for AI?
options: A highly fragmented market with hundreds of competitive AI models each serving a different specialized niche and use case
A monopoly or oligopoly where the top few frontier models dominate because users always prefer the smartest
A market where open-source models eventually surpass proprietary ones through cumulative community contributions and peer review
A market where every company fine-tunes its own proprietary model and no single player achieves dominant market share
answer: A monopoly or oligopoly where the top few frontier models dominate because users always prefer the smartest
explanation: Naval says: 'Which isn't great news, because it means you'll end up creating a monopoly or oligopoly situation in AI. But I always want the most intelligent programmer.'

question: The Intelligence Unicorn
content: Guillermo reveals that Chinese models are 'certainly not in it' when it comes to frontier coding â€” despite all the hype, the real frontier work is dominated by just two or three Western model providers.
description: A tech journalist claims 'Chinese AI models are now competing head-to-head with Western frontier models on coding tasks.' Based on what Naval and Guillermo agree on, is this claim accurate?
options: Yes, DeepSeek has surpassed GPT-4 on all major coding benchmarks and is now the undisputed leader in AI programming
No â€” neither Naval nor Guillermo sees Chinese models being used for frontier coding work
Partially — Chinese models lead on practical coding tasks but still trail significantly on creative and open-ended writing
The comparison is fundamentally meaningless because Chinese model providers do not publish standardized benchmark results
answer: No â€” neither Naval nor Guillermo sees Chinese models being used for frontier coding work
explanation: Naval says he doesn't know anyone who uses Chinese models. Guillermo confirms: 'The Chinese are certainly not in it' when it comes to frontier coding. Chinese models find use in support and automation, not cutting-edge coding.
